Rumors have long suggested that Apple is preparing an all-glass new device design for the 20th anniversary of the iPhone next year. However, an analyst at Jefferies believes that the device is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analyst says bold iPhone 20th anniversary redesign has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple stock to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that the possible cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons.

The key to this downgrade lies in the suspected cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although the project was reported to be under development as early as 2025, with rumors suggesting an earliest launch in 2027, Apple has never commented on the speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent application for a "six-sided glass enclosure" as early as 2019. Jefferies had previously believed that launching an all-glass iPhone was possible, but Lee thinks development work has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply chain checks indicate the project was cancelled due to low yield rates. Lee believes this decision is "a major setback for driving higher-priced iPhone launches amid soaring memory prices." If the device launches in September 2027 to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, he estimates the blended retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further increasing their average selling prices and profits." He believes that amid rising memory prices, this move would have been a key defensive strategy.

Lee also pointed to Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro as reasons for the further downgrade of the company's stock rating.

From Lee's report, it is unclear whether the analyst believes the entire redesign has been shelved, or only some elements of it have been cancelled.

Top comment posted by Currentinterest

These analysts have been wrong multiple times with their predictions about Apple's future plans. Even the term "all-glass" may have never accurately reflected what Apple truly wanted to do. The 20th anniversary phone will be innovative, and there will be market demand for it, regardless of the final design.

For example, rumors have long indicated that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an "all-glass" display is simply not feasible. However, the rumored four-curved-edge design may still launch.

In any case, if Apple's iPhone 20th anniversary design has really been cancelled, we should soon get confirmation from other credible sources.

What are your thoughts on this report about the iPhone 20th anniversary design? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
